questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Introduces federated learning for on-device NLP in multilingual settings, testing privacy, compute, and evaluation constraints beyond single-device inference.

## Key Concepts
- Federated learning, secure aggregation, differential privacy
- On-device NLP, quantization, small architectures
- Multilingual subword vocabularies, transfer learning
- Evaluation in offline and simulated FL settings

## Code Example
```javascript
# Pseudocode: Federated Averaging loop
global_model = init()
for round in rounds:
  updates = []
  for client in random_clients:
    local = train(client.data, global_model)
    updates.append(local - global_model)
  global_model += avg(updates, secure=True, dp_epsilon=1.0)
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you quantify privacy leakage and mitigation effectiveness in this FL setup?
- What trade-offs arise from adding differential privacy noise on low-memory devices?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests on-device NLP design, privacy guarantees, and multilingual handling with code-switching in a beginner-friendly setting. Assesses ability to blend regex-based detection with a compact NER model and plan labeling, rollout, and evaluation.

## Key Concepts

- On-device inference with WebAssembly
- PII detection: regex patterns + lightweight NER
- Multilingual and code-switching resilience
- Privacy guarantees and staged rollout
- Evaluation metrics: precision/recall for redactions

## Code Example

```javascript
function redactPII(text) {
  const email = /\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b/g;
  const phone = /\b(\+?\d{1,3}[-.\s+]?)?(\(?\d{2,4}\)?[-.\s+]?\d{3,4}[-.\s+]?\d{3,4})\b/g;
  return text
    .replace(email, "[REDACTED_EMAIL]")
    .replace(phone, "[REDACTED_PHONE]");
}
```

- How would you extend to additional languages?
